# ThaiMusicXML

> An open, royalty-free XML file format for Thai traditional music (เพลงไทยเดิม / Phleng Thai Doem).

ThaiMusicXML records the notation Thai musicians already read - the 7-tone scale (ด ร ม ฟ ซ ล ท) as
scale degrees rather than fixed pitches, the beat grid that aligns every instrument down the page,
rests that mean "no new stroke" rather than silence, unpitched rows for ฉิ่ง and other percussion,
lyrics, bow and gesture curves, cued passages, and repeat marks - in a form software can validate,
search, print, and hand to another program without tying the score to any one editor. It is
published under Apache License 2.0.

Documentation is available in English (`/en/`) and Thai (`/th/`). Every URL below is the English
page; swap `/en/` for `/th/` for the Thai translation.

## Getting started

- [ThaiMusicXML](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/): An open, royalty-free XML format for Thai traditional music (เพลงไทยเดิม). Records the 7-tone scale ด ร ม ฟ ซ ล ท, the beat grid, and what a musician reads.
- [ThaiMusicXML v1.0](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/introduction/): ThaiMusicXML v1.0 covers pitched, unpitched, and lyric parts; ท่อน with repeats and endings; octave dots, subdivided beats, curves, and cued passages.
- [Playground](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/playground/): Write and validate ThaiMusicXML in the browser, with live score rendering

## Tutorial

- [Hello World](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/tutorial/1-hello_world/): Your first ThaiMusicXML file
- [File Structure](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/tutorial/2-file_structure/): How ThaiMusicXML files are organized
- [The score model](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/tutorial/3-the_score_model/): How ThaiMusicXML represents time, beats, and rests
- [Notes, rests, and octaves](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/tutorial/4-notes_and_octaves/): Pitch names, octave marks, and the rest element
- [Beats and subdivision](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/tutorial/5-beats_and_subdivision/): How groups split a beat into equal parts
- [Sections, repeats, and endings](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/tutorial/6-sections_repeats_endings/): How scores organize sections and handle repeats
- [Ensembles and stacked instruments](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/tutorial/7-ensembles_stacked/): Multiple parts, stacked rows, and parts that sit out
- [Lyrics and chords](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/tutorial/8-lyrics/): Vocal parts, syllables, the counting rule, and chord symbols on their own row
- [Marking the score](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/tutorial/9-marking_the_score/): Spans, annotations, credits, and metadata
- [Validating and going further](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/tutorial/10-validating/): Schema validation, the Playground, and where to go next

## Elements

- [Elements Reference](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/): Every element in a ThaiMusicXML v1.0 document and how they nest, from <thai-score> down through <header>, <structure>, <ensemble>, and <part-data>.
- [<annotation>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/annotation/): A free-form comment ignored during playback. Its scope comes from where it sits: the whole score, one part's section, or a single line.
- [<arranger>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/arranger/): Names whoever produced this setting of the piece. Much of the repertoire is traditional, so a score often has no composer but a known arranger.
- [<bow>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/bow/): Marks a span of notes played with one continuous bow stroke, without changing direction. A span may cross measures and lines, but not sections.
- [<bpm>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/bpm/): Sets the tempo in beats per minute, where one bpm beat is half a measure. Every measure lasts the same time whatever its beat count.
- [<br>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/br/): A line break between the annotations and directions that make up a score's structure.
- [<chan>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/chan/): Sets the ชั้น (chan) rhythmic layer, which determines rhythmic density. One of five levels, from ครึ่งชั้น through ชั้นเดียว, สองชั้น, สามชั้น, to สี่ชั้น.
- [<chord>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/chord/): One chord symbol, written the way it should print, in a part whose type is chord. Symbols flush right against the end of the measure.
- [<composer>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/composer/): Identifies the composer or attribution of the piece. The text prints exactly as typed, centered, or split into up to three aligned runs.
- [<direction>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/direction/): Carries performance directions for the score: the หน้าทับ cycle, the ชั้น layer, and the tempo in beats per minute.
- [<ending>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/ending/): Replaces specific lines on specific passes of a repeated section, so one part can play a variation without restructuring its section.
- [<ensemble>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/ensemble/): Lists the instruments in the score. Parts render in the order given here, with the rows of a stacked instrument kept together.
- [<group>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/group/): Subdivides a single beat into two or more equal parts, for measures that pack more notes into a beat than usual.
- [<header>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/header/): Score metadata: what the piece is called, who is behind it, what tuning it is written against, and the terms it is published under.
- [<instrument-name>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/instrument-name/): Names an instrument, in English or Thai. On one row of a stacked instrument it names the hand too, as in ฆ้องวงใหญ่ มือขวา.
- [<instrument-short-name>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/instrument-short-name/): A shortened form of the instrument name, for wherever the full name does not fit. Optional, and parts without one fall back to the full name.
- [<license>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/license/): States the terms the score is published under. The terms cover the transcription as a document, not the traditional music it records.
- [<line>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/line/): A musical line (บรรทัด) within one part's section, holding one to eight measures. Nine or more is a validation error.
- [<line-repeat>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/line-repeat/): Repeats a consecutive range of lines within a section, without repeating the section as a whole.
- [<link>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/link/): Marks a span of notes as one connected gesture, สะบัด, and asks for a curve drawn above the notation saying so.
- [<lyricist>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/lyricist/): Names whoever wrote the words to the piece. The text prints exactly as typed, centered, or split into up to three aligned runs.
- [<measure>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/measure/): A single measure (ห้อง) holding one part's notes and rests, or its words or chord symbols. Every notated part agrees on how many beats a given measure has.
- [<nathap>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/nathap/): Names the หน้าทับ drum cycle the music is set against, which fixes the length of the cycle and the pattern of strokes inside it.
- [<note>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/note/): One attack in a part. A pitched part writes a scale degree from ด ร ม ฟ ซ ล ท with an octave mark; an unpitched part writes a sound code.
- [<parenthesis>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/parenthesis/): Marks a span of notes and rests as cued rather than played, where the part waits for another instrument to carry the passage.
- [<part>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/part/): Declares that a part exists in the ensemble, with its type, name, and whether it stacks with another row. It holds no notes.
- [<part-data>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/part-data/): Holds the music for a single instrument. A part declares that the instrument exists; part-data is where its notes actually live.
- [<play>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/play/): Plays a section again later in the score, taking another place in the play order without a second copy of its music.
- [<repeat>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/repeat/): Wraps a run of the score's structure and plays it more than once. Repeats nest, so a piece can be built from layers of them.
- [<rest>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/rest/): One beat on which the instrument plays nothing new. Thai instruments have no notated sustain, so a rest is no attack rather than silence.
- [<section>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/section/): Declares that a named section of the score exists and where it falls in the play order. It holds no notes.
- [<section-ref>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/section-ref/): Holds one part's music for a section the score's structure declared, as lines of measures, plus any variant endings.
- [<structure>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/structure/): Defines the score layout: which sections are played, in what order, how often, and with what directions along the way.
- [<syllable>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/syllable/): One syllable of เนื้อร้อง, written the way it should be read, in a part whose type is lyric.
- [<text>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/text/): One aligned run of text inside an annotation or a credit, claiming the left, center, or right of its parent's single line.
- [<thai-score>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/thai-score/): The root element of every ThaiMusicXML document, carrying the namespace and the schema version the file follows.
- [<title>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/title/): The title of the musical piece. Exactly one is required in every score header.
- [<tuning>](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/elements/tuning/): States what absolute pitch the scale degrees stand for. Without it a score says what to play relative to the ensemble, but not at what pitch.

## Examples

- [Examples](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/examples/): Complete ThaiMusicXML scores of real repertoire, each one annotated with the elements and concepts it demonstrates.
- [Homrong Chom Surang](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/examples/chomsurang/): A single-line score for the โหมโรง piece โหมโรงจอมสุรางค์
- [Chuen Chumnum - Klum Dontri](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/examples/chuen-chumnum/): A single-part ซออู้ score for two short สองชั้น pieces
- [Khaek Borathes](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/examples/khaek-borathes/): A three-instrument score for แขกบรเทศ ชั้นเดียว
- [Sathukan](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/examples/sathukan/): A two-row ฆ้องวงใหญ่ transcription of the หน้าพาทย์ piece สาธุการ

## Reference

- [Conformance](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/conformance/): What it means for a document or a processor to conform to ThaiMusicXML v1.0
- [Conversion](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/conversion/): How a ThaiMusicXML document maps to other notation and playback formats
- [Rendering](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/rendering/): Non-normative guidance for laying out and displaying a ThaiMusicXML score
- [Schema and test suite](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/reference/schema/): The RELAX NG schema for ThaiMusicXML v1.0 and the conformance corpus that goes with it

## Updates

- [Breaking Changes](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/updates/breaking-changes/): Incompatible changes between ThaiMusicXML versions, and what a document or processor has to do about each one.
- [Overview](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/updates/erratum/): Corrections published against the ThaiMusicXML v1.0 specification after its release.
- [Overview](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/updates/roadmap/): What ThaiMusicXML v1.0 covers, what is deliberately out of scope, and what is planned for later versions.

## Project

- [About ThaiMusicXML](https://thaimusicxml.anan.ovh/en/about/): What ThaiMusicXML records and why: scale degrees over fixed pitches, the eight-measure grid, rests as no new stroke, and the debt the format owes MusicXML.
